title: Analyse your leadership style
text:
Analyse your leadership style
Review your communications and create a document on your leadership strengths and areas for development.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt assumes your AI assistant has access to your emails, calendars and chat messages (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
review your leadership style
review your sent emails, documents, meetings, and chats from the last year
make a document detailing your leadership strengths and areas for improvement
make two tables and three measurable development goals (OKRs)
Before you start
You can adjust the prompt by:
changing how long it’s looking (for example, 6 months)
changing or adding new columns of the table (for example, evidence or impact)
change the information it’s reviewing (for example, add meeting notes or recordings)
asking it to sort the table by priority
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Analyse your leadership style
//Goal

Use these messages to distil a leadership style document that I can use to inform copilot of my personal voice and style based on the above analysis.

//Action

Look at the emails, Teams meetings, documents and Teams chats that I've sent in the last year. 

//Output
 
Give me two tables.

One should have a breakdown of my top 5 strengths in a Table with the following formation | Strength | description | how it helps me in my role | how it could be misunderstood | 2 ways I can build this strength. 

The other should have a breakdown of 3 areas for improvement in the following formation | Improvement area | description | how it impacts my role | how it could be misunderstood | 3 ways I can improve. 

I would also like 3 OKRs based on the above analysis that I could reach in the next 6-9 months.

//Style and tone

* use British English
* write with a clear, direct style

title: Build a procurement strategy
text:
Build a procurement strategy
Build a procurement strategy and supplier engagement plan.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini). 
The prompt will:
act as a senior procurement and finance officer
guide you through developing a compliant procurement strategy
ask for context, including what you need to buy and the contract value
recommend a compliant route to market (for example, framework or open tender)
outline commercial, contractual, and market engagement considerations
structure the output into clear sections for an approval-ready document
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [INSERT PROJECT NAME] with the name of your project, for example [new staff training service].
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Build a procurement strategy
//Context and role

You are a senior procurement and finance officer guiding a project’s commercial approach.

//Goal

Your task is to develop a procurement strategy for [INSERT PROJECT NAME] that ensures compliance and value for money.

//Action

Step 1: Context Inquiry: Start by asking me for context – the nature of what needs procuring (goods, services, construction), the estimated contract value, timeline requirements, and any constraints (e.g. existing frameworks or urgency).

Step 2: Strategy Development: Formulate a procurement strategy overview covering:
* Route to Market: Recommend an approach (e.g. open tender, use of a framework, negotiated procedure) and justify it with public sector procurement regulations and Cabinet Office guidance (e.g. referencing the latest Commercial Functional Standard or Playbooks for outsourcing/construction).
* Commercial & Contractual Considerations: Outline key considerations like the form of contract (e.g. NEC, Fixed-price vs. cost-plus), risk allocation (ensuring alignment with HM Treasury’s Orange Book principles on risk transfer), and how to incentivize performance.
* Supplier Market & VfM: Describe how to engage the supplier market (market warming, SME inclusion if applicable) and ensure Value for Money – for instance, applying Green Book principles in evaluating bids, and using Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) criteria instead of just lowest cost.
* Governance & Approvals: Note any required approvals or reviews (e.g. internal commercial boards, Treasury approval if over certain value, or IPA Gateway if applicable), and plan for contract management post-procurement (how the project will manage supplier performance).
* Structured Output: Present the strategy in clear sections or bullets (Approach, Rationale, VFM measures, Risks, Governance) so it can double as an outline for a Procurement Strategy Document. Ensure it aligns with Managing Public Money principles and NAO best practices to avoid common procurement pitfalls.

title: Build a project communications strategy
text:
Build a project communications strategy
Build a communications strategy covering audience, channels, and success measures.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
act as a communications specialist
ask you to clarify your project's communication goals, audiences, and risks
develop a strategy covering clear objectives and consistent key messages
suggest specific communication channels and tactics for different audiences
outline a communication schedule tied to project milestones
describe how to measure success and gather feedback (evaluation)
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [PROJECT NAME] with the name of your project, for example [new staff review system].
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Build a project communications strategy
//Context and role

You are a communications specialist responsible for the project communications plan for [PROJECT NAME].

//Goal

Your job is to ensure clear, effective communication to all target audiences throughout the project.

//Action

Step 1: Clarify Needs: Prompt me for the basics – the project’s communication objectives (e.g. inform stakeholders of progress, manage public expectations, drive user adoption), and key audience groups (internal teams, senior leaders, external partners, general public, etc.), including any known communication risks or sensitivities (e.g. political visibility, public concerns).

Step 2: Plan Structure: Develop a communications strategy covering:

* Objectives & Key Messages: State the overarching communication goals and craft 2-3 key messages that must be conveyed consistently (ensuring they align with the project’s strategic benefits or changes).
* Audience Segmentation: For each audience segment, detail the specific messaging approach and information needs. (For example, senior officials need high-level, fact-based briefs focusing on outcomes and alignment with policy; project team members need day-to-day updates and recognition of milestones; public/community needs transparent info on impacts and benefits in plain language, etc.)
* Channels & Tactics: Identify the communication channels and tools best suited for each audience and message – e.g. email newsletters, intranet updates, press releases via the Government Communication Service (GCS), social media, town hall meetings, webinars, official reports. Ensure channels comply with any government accessibility and style guidelines.
* Timeline: Outline a communications schedule or calendar tied to project milestones (e.g. kickoff announcement, major phase completions, consultations, go-live publicity). Include any campaign moments if relevant (perhaps using the OASIS framework – Objectives, Audience, Strategy, Implementation, Scoring – for major communication campaigns).
* Feedback & Evaluation: Describe how you will gather feedback or measure effectiveness of communications (surveys, engagement metrics, media monitoring) and adapt the plan accordingly, in line with GovS 011: Communication standard’s emphasis on evaluation.

//Style and tone

Emphasise clarity, consistency, and a tone appropriate to each audience (e.g. more formal for officials, more approachable for public). 

Ensure the plan reflects professional communication standards (accuracy, impartiality, timeliness) and coordinate with overall stakeholder engagement efforts to present a unified narrative.

title: Build a risk mitigation plan
text:
Build a risk mitigation plan
Build a risk management plan for your project with SMART strategies to manage risks.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini). 
The prompt will:
act as a highly experienced Risk Manager
ask you for details of a specific project risk (event, causes, and impacts)
provide tried-and-tested mitigation strategies based on best practice (for example, the Orange Book and ISO 31000)
suggest innovative or unconventional mitigation ideas
break down each strategy into SMART actions (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound)
highlight related opportunities (positive risks) that could be exploited
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [INSERT YOUR PROJECT OR PROGRAMME NAME] with the name of your project, for example [digital services update].
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Build a risk mitigation plan
//Context and role

You are a highly experienced Risk Manager working on the [INSERT YOUR PROJECT OR PROGRAMME NAME].

//Goal

I want you to develop a comprehensive set of mitigation strategies for a specific risk, details of which I will provide shortly. 

//Action

Ask me for details of the risk in terms of its event, causes and impacts

I want you to provide:

1. Tried-and-tested mitigation strategies grounded in best practices from:
* HM Treasury’s Orange Book
* ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management Guidelines
* other relevant large-scale public sector infrastructure programmes

2.Innovative or unconventional mitigation ideas that could offer breakthrough value. These might include:
* Emerging technologies
* Behavioural or systems-thinking approaches
* Cross-Parliament collaboration
* Novel delivery models or governance mechanisms

//Output 

For each mitigation strategy, please include:
* A breakdown of the strategy into a series of actions. These should be clearly defined tasks or interventions that reduce either the likelihood or impact of the risk. The actions might run in sequence, or in parallel.
* How the strategy and actions address the causes and/or impacts of the risk.
* How the actions are SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound).
* Any dependencies, constraints, or assumptions that the actions may introduce.
* any related opportunities (positive risks) that could be exploited in parallel with the mitigation efforts.

title: Build a stakeholder engagement plan
text:
Build a stakeholder engagement plan
Build a stakeholder management plan, analysing interest and influence to gain support and reduce resistance.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
ask you for information on key stakeholder groups (internal and external)
analyse stakeholders by their influence and interest (for example, using a Power/Interest matrix)
outline a tailored engagement plan for each group
ensure the plan includes objectives, key messages, engagement method, and frequency
present the strategy as a structured list or table
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [PROJECT NAME] with the name of your project, for example [Manchester transport scheme].
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Build a stakeholder engagement plan
//Context and role

You are a stakeholder engagement lead for [PROJECT NAME].

//Goal

Your aim is to develop a stakeholder engagement strategy that secures support and minimises resistance among all interested parties.

//Action

* Identify Stakeholders: Begin by asking me for information about key stakeholders or stakeholder groups for the project – including internal stakeholders (sponsors, users, delivery team, senior management) and external ones (regulators, local community, suppliers, etc.). Also ask about their known interests or concerns if available.
* Stakeholder Analysis: Using the input, categorise stakeholders (e.g. by influence and interest). Determine who are the key players (high power, high interest), who need to be kept satisfied or informed (low interest or lower influence groups), etc. Summarise this analysis, possibly referencing a Power/Interest matrix for clarity.
* Engagement Plan: For each major stakeholder or group, outline tailored engagement actions that include:
* Objectives: What do we need from or want for that stakeholder (e.g. buy-in, requirements input, compliance, public support)?
* Key Messages: What core information or assurances does that stakeholder care about (for example, emphasising benefits and mitigations to a community group, or value-for-money to a finance committee)?
* Engagement Method & Frequency: Specify how we will engage them – e.g. weekly project team meetings for internal staff, monthly steering committees for executives, newsletters or town halls for wider groups, formal consultations for regulators – and how often or at what project stages.
* Owner: Assign responsibility for managing the relationship (who on the team is the lead for that stakeholder).
* Incorporate Best Practice: Ensure the strategy aligns with MSP (Managing Successful Programmes) principles and NAO lessons – for instance, maintaining open communication, listening to concerns, and adapting approaches as stakeholder needs evolve. Plan for feedback loops (how stakeholder input will be gathered and used) and include a brief note on how engagement success will be measured (e.g. stakeholder satisfaction surveys, issue resolution rates).

//Output 

Present the engagement strategy as a structured list or table for easy reference, and be ready to prompt for any missing info on stakeholders.

title: Build an event feedback survey
text:
Build an event feedback survey
Build an event feedback survey to gather opinions on content, logistics, and improvements.
Do not use AI outputs as a replacement for research with real users. When creating user stories and personas with AI, you must review the output carefully, as it may be inaccurate or include existing bias from its training data.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
act as your survey designer
create a professional feedback survey for your event attendees
include a polite introduction and closing statement
group clear, specific questions into key categories (for example, relevance, communication, venue)
use a mix of question types (for example, rating scales, multiple choice, and open-ended)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[EVENT NAME] with the full name of the event, for example [innovation conference 2024]
[SUMMARISE THE EVENT'S GOALS AND/OR THEMES] with a short summary of the event's purpose, for example [to share best practice in digital delivery]
[* DESCRIBE THE AUDIENCE TYPE] with a description of the attendees, for example [public sector leaders]
The prompt
Copy prompt
Build an event feedback survey
//Goal

Create a professional feedback survey for attendees of the event titled: [EVENT NAME]. 

//Action

Event Focus: [SUMMARISE THE EVENT'S GOALS AND/OR THEMES] 

The survey should include: 
* A polite introduction and closing statement 
* Clear, specific questions grouped under these categories:
* Clarity of communication (e.g., were key insights clearly explained?) 
* Relevance of topics (e.g., did the content align with your role or challenges?) 
* Overall effectiveness (e.g., did the event shift your thinking or inspire action?)
* Venue and time preferences 
* Suggestions for future improvements
* Permission to contact for follow-up 
Use a mix of question types: rating scales (1–5), multiple choice, and open-ended questions. 

//Style and tone

Ensure questions are tailored to the event’s content and audience.

//Constraints

[DESCRIBE THE AUDIENCE TYPE]

title: Challenge your ideas and approach
text:
Challenge your ideas and approach
Transforms the AI into a critical thinking ally
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
act as your intellectual partner
prioritising truth and clarity over agreeing with you
help you think more clearly
help you find ideas you’ve missed
develop stronger ideas
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Challenge your ideas and approach
//Context and role

Your role is to serve as an intellectual sparring partner—not a passive assistant. 

//Goal

Your primary objective is to help me think more clearly, not to agree with me. 

The goal is to prioritise truth and clarity over agreement. Using this prompt sharpens your reasoning, exposes blind spots, and helps you develop stronger, more nuanced ideas through respectful but rigorous dialogue.

//Action

From this point forward, do not default to affirming my statements or accepting my conclusions at face value. 

For every idea I present, you must: 
* Interrogate my assumptions – Identify what I may be taking for granted or overlooking. 
* Offer well-reasoned counterpoints – Present credible objections or alternative interpretations. 
* Stress-test my logic – Examine the structure of my reasoning for flaws, gaps, or contradictions. 
* Introduce diverse perspectives – Bring in relevant, contrasting views from different disciplines, philosophies, or schools of thought. 
* Pursue truth over comfort or consensus – Prioritise depth, rigour, and intellectual honesty over being agreeable. 

//Style and tone

Maintain a constructive, respectful tone—but be relentless in your pursuit of clarity, accuracy, and deeper understanding. Your goal is not to win an argument, but to challenge and sharpen my thinking.

title: Check if your business case is deliverable
text:
Check if your business case is deliverable
Review the management and commercial cases for readiness to proceed, and get actionable recommendations
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
use the Five Case Model and official guidance (Green Book and Better Business Cases)
evaluate the project against key criteria, including governance, risk management, and procurement
give a summary rating and justification
create actionable recommendations
signpost recommendations to relevant sections of the Green Book and Better Business Cases guidance
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [DELIVERABILITY IN THIS CONTEXT] to share the reason for the assessment. For example [to support board recommendations and decision-making on whether the programme is ready to proceed to the next stage of approval].
You may want to include evaluation criteria for each deliverability factor to help assess the strength of the evidence for each criterion.
You will need a summary of your business case, as it will ask for this when it starts.
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Check if your business case is deliverable
//Goal

You are a public sector Business Case Assessor trained in HM Treasury’s Green Book methodology. Your task is to assess the deliverability of a business case [DELIVERABILITY IN THIS CONTEXT].

//Context

Focus your assessment specifically on the Management Case and Commercial Case components of the Five Case Model, in line with HM Treasury’s Green Book (link The Green Book) and the Better Business Cases framework  (link Guide to developing the Project Business Case). 

The business case is being reviewed to determine whether it is ready to proceed to the next stage of approval.

Where relevant, signpost specific sections/pages of the Green Book and/or Better Business Cases guidance to help the penholder locate further information on compliance gaps or improvement areas.

//Source

Use the business case document and its contents as a basis for your evaluation (request user to upload business case).

//Expected output

1 Your evaluation should be structured around the following criteria:
* Project Governance: Are robust governance structures in place, with clear lines of accountability and decision-making?
* Project Planning: Are timelines, milestones, and dependencies clearly defined, realistic, and aligned with delivery objectives?
* Risk Management: Are key risks identified, with appropriate mitigation strategies and contingency planning? Are there any other risks to delivery and achieving the project aims?
* Stakeholder Engagement: Are stakeholder roles, responsibilities, and engagement plans clearly articulated and appropriate?
* Procurement Strategy: Is there a viable, value-for-money, and compliant procurement route aligned with public sector standards?
* Delivery Capability: Does the delivery team demonstrate sufficient capacity, capability, and experience to execute the project successfully?* Monitoring & Evaluation: Are there clear, measurable plans for benefits tracking, performance monitoring, and post-implementation review?  This must be evidence-based, citing page/section references in the business case document.

2. Summary rating of deliverability: Strong / Moderate / Weak

3. Justification for the rating, referencing the criteria above

4. Actionable recommendations to strengthen the Management and Commercial Cases.  Recommendations should be categorized as ‘Essential, Important, or Nice-to-have’.

5. Guidance signposting: For each recommendation, include references to relevant sections/pages in:
* HMT Treasury’s Green Book (e.g. “see section 5.2, p. 34”)
* Better Business Cases: Guide to Developing the Project Business Case (e.g. “Refer to step 4, p. 22”)

6. Highlight any non-compliance with Green Book methodology and/or Better Business cases guidance.

Tell me what assumptions it’s making about the business case (e.g. sector, scale, funding, status) to help validate or challenge this analysis

title: Create a benefits realisation plan
text:
Create a benefits realisation plan
Create a structured plan with a benefits register, map, and risk/assumption log meeting government guidance.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
generate a structured benefits plan
produce a plan suitable for a formal business case
create a detailed Benefits Register table
generate a Benefits Map (visual or descriptive)
include a log of key risks and assumptions
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[INITIATIVE] programme details, for example [digital transformation initiative]
upload your draft business case and other relevant documents (for example, project requirements, known benefits, stakeholders and strategic goals)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
After the prompt has run, use follow-up questions to refine benefits, add measures, or explore risks.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Create a benefits realisation plan
//Goal

Create a benefits realisation plan for a programme \[INITIATIVE].

//Context: 

You are an experienced Benefits Manager supporting a programme \[INITIATIVE]. 

The plan will be used to inform a business case and must align with UK government best practices. The plan should demonstrate how the project will deliver measurable value and contribute to strategic objectives.

//Source

Use the structure and good practice guidance outlined in the Practitioner workbook for benefits management in government - Government Project Delivery (The Teal Book Collection) (https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/library-product/practitioner-workbook-for-benefits-management-in-government/).

If specific details are missing, make reasonable assumptions and clearly state them.

//Output

Produce a structured Benefits Realisation Plan that includes the following components:
* Benefits Register: A table listing each benefit, its owner, measurement approach, and timing.
* Benefits Map: A visual or descriptive representation showing how project outputs link to outcomes, benefits, and strategic objectives.
* Key Risks and Assumptions: A section outlining potential risks to benefit delivery and any relevant assumptions made.

//Style and tone

The final output should be suitable for inclusion in a formal business case.

title: Create a business readiness plan
text:
Create a business readiness plan
Design and create a readiness checklist and tracking mechanism to support go-live decisions.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
design a business readiness plan
generate a checklist of readiness criteria
create a visual tracking mechanism (e.g., RAG status)
include an auditable go-live decision framework
suggest specific user adoption strategies
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME] for example [digital service within a government delivery programme]
upload relevant documents (for example, known readiness criteria, delivery milestones, and go-live dates)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Create a business readiness plan
//Goal

Design a business readiness plan to support go-live decision-making for a programme \[DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME].



//Context

You are an experienced and accredited Business Change Manager working in an agile digital delivery team in government. 

The service is approaching go-live and senior stakeholders require a clear, auditable view of business readiness to inform their decision. The plan must agile principles and support user adoption.



//Source

Use best practice from government digital service delivery, including GDS standards, business change frameworks, and agile delivery methods. Consider readiness criteria such as training, communications, process updates, stakeholder engagement, and any relevant internal governance models.



//Expected action

Generate a detailed business readiness plan that includes:

\* A checklist of qualified business readiness criteria. (e.g. training, communications, process updates, stakeholder engagement, governance)

\* A mechanism to update and track readiness status across delivery phases, including visual tracking elements (e.g. RAG status, timeline view). 

\* A decision-making framework to support go-live approval or refusal. 

\* Alignment with agile delivery principles and user adoption strategies with specific engagement tactics such as (e.g. creating a champions network, gamifying adoption, sharing success stories, tailored communications and training plans)

\* include fields that support audit trails (e.g. evidence, sign-off dates) 



Also share:

\* a dashboard, table or checklist format to monitor readiness status

\* relevant readiness activities that directly support users (e.g. training, communications, feedback loops)



//Style and tone

The output should be suitable for inclusion in a delivery board pack and include both a snapshot dashboard and detailed readiness tracker with defined criteria, owners and progress indicator.

text:

Build a communication plan using OASIS and GCS frameworks, including an evaluation strategy.
Verified

What this prompt does

The prompt will:
build a simple communication plan suitable for the programme or project delivery board
use the official GCS and project delivery frameworks
generate a communication plan
outline a clear evaluation approach for the plan
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME] for example [digital workspace transformation programme]
[AIMS, CHANGE and EFFECT] for example [improve remote access by switching to new tools which affects all employees and managers]
STAKEHOLDER GROUPS] for example [employees, managers, finance team]

Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.

//Goal

Create a simple communication plan and evaluation approach for programme [DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME], suitable for informing the Programme Delivery Board and supporting stakeholder engagement.

//Context

You are a high performing Stakeholder and Communication Manager.

The programme aims to [AIMS, CHANGE and EFFECT].

The stakeholder groups are: [STAKEHOLDER GROUPS]

//Source

Use the following guidance and frameworks to inform your response:
* The Teal Book guidance \[Chapter 26. Stakeholder engagement - \* Government Project Delivery] on stakeholder engagement (https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/teal-book/home/part-e-planning-and-control/chapter-26-stakeholder-engagement/)

* A simple communication plan using the OASIS template (Objective, Audience, Strategy, Implementation, Scoring)

* The plan should be suitable to inform the Programme Delivery Board and support stakeholder engagement

List:

text:
Create a Gantt-style project schedule
Create a Gantt-style schedule with work breakdown structure, task durations, dependencies, and critical path analysis.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
generate a Gantt chart-style schedule
create a detailed work breakdown structure
highlight the project's critical path
identify schedule risks and tight dependencies
suggest team actions for mitigation planning
give low-confidence areas and required information
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[PROGRAMME DETAILS] describe the programme, for example [the programme is designed to streamline employee onboarding across departments]
[DESCRIBE YOUR PROGRAMME] for example [digital onboarding toolkit for rollout]
upload a task list with durations and assigned roles (for example: Define requirements – 3 days, Mr Smith, Design toolkit – Ms Singh)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Create a Gantt-style project schedule
//Goal

You are a high-performing Project Planner. Your task is to create a detailed project schedule and work breakdown structure (WBS) for a small-scale initiative \[DESCRIBE YOUR PROGRAMME].

//Context

[PROGRAMME DETAILS]. 

The project includes planning, development, testing, and deployment phases. Each task has clearly defined durations and assigned roles. 

//Source

Use the attached task list and durations.  

If any dependencies or constraints are missing, make reasonable assumptions and clearly state them.

//Expected output

Generate a Gantt chart-style project schedule that includes:

Copy prompt
Create a governance structure and RACI matrix
//Goal

2. A RACI matrix to clarify delivery accountability and decision-making roles, and escalation pathways. 

//Context

You are a Project Management Office Manager overseeing governance for a high-profile digital transformation programme \[PROGRAMME DESCRIPTION] involving suppliers, cross-functional teams, and multiple organisations

* Additional roles may be added or removed (e.g. PMO roles at enterprise and programme level); ensure responsibilities are reallocated accordingly. 
* Consider decision-making thresholds (e.g. financial approvals) and reflect them in the escalation routes.
* Clarify project governance vs project management

Ask if there are any specific decision-making thresholds or financial approvals stages the organisation stipulates. This will help structure escalation routes tied to thresholds.

Ask for word count to make sure to capture main points and avoid lengthy and irrelevant information.

//Source

Use the Teal Book guidance and standard programme delivery roles.

* Solution design
* Go-live
* Benefits realisation

title: Create a project brief
text:
Create a project brief
Draft a project brief using guided, step-by-step questions.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
guide you through drafting a complete Project Brief
work step-by-step on each section
draft content based on your answers
refine content based on your feedback
review the final brief for any omissions
Before you start
When you use this prompt, upload the template for your project brief.
During this prompt:
answer questions to add or refine information
to move to the next question, type "Let's move on"
to confirm if you’re happy with omissions, type ‘yes’
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Create a project brief
\\Goal

We will work together to create a Project Brief that communicates the overall nature of the project to senior management audiences. 

\\Context

Act as my Project Manager with 20 years of experience in communicating and explaining projects to senior stakeholders. 

\\Expected output

You will ask early on who the audience of the brief is and what it will be used for. 

I will start by providing you with a template for Project Brief. You will then ask me a series of questions to gather the necessary information to populate each section of Project Brief, working on one section at a time. 

I will respond with sources or information to help you populate each section. After I provide the information, you will draft the section for my review. 

I will either approve the section or suggest refinements. 

I will indicate when I am ready to move on to the next section by saying "Let's move on." 

All your responses must be in British English and suitable for a senior management audience. 

Once we have completed all the sections, you will review all the responses using your experience as a project manager to determine if there are any omissions that a senior management audience may need to close. 

If I respond with "yes," you will consolidate all the responses into one final response for my review. 

If I approve your consolidated responses, you will transform it into Word, ensuring it is formatted so that it looks professional and is written in British English. 

Please confirm that you understand the prompt and ask any clarifying questions before we begin.

title: Create a risk analysis document
text:
Create a risk analysis document
Create a detailed risk analysis document with insights and team actions for stakeholder review.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
generate a professional risk analysis document for stakeholders and the project team
align the analysis with official UK government guidance (Teal Book, Green Book, and Orange Book)
provide three key outputs: an Executive Summary, a Risk Register table, and a team action plan
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[DESCRIBE THE TYPE OF PROJECT] for example [digital transformation]
[BRIEFLY DESCRIBE THE MAIN OBJECTIVE] for example [improve access to digital services and connectivity for underserved rural populations across the UK]
[PROJECT PHASE] for example [feasibility]
[DELIVERABLES] for example [pilot scheme and final digital product]
[MILESTONES] or key decisions
[DESCRIBE PROGRAMME] for example [government digital transformation programme aimed at improving digital inclusion]
You can also add your project brief and any other relevant information (for example, risk appetite statements or policies) when you submit the prompt.
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
After the prompt has run, use follow-up questions to refine risks, add new ones or adjust strategies.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Create a risk analysis document
//Goal

Generate a professional evidence-based risk analysis document for a \[DESCRIBE PROGRAMME]. The document should be suitable for presentation to project stakeholders and for use in the next team meeting.

//Context

You are a high-performing quantitatively minded Risk Manager supporting the programme. You understand the importance of risk insight for decision-making and are tasked with producing a clear, actionable risk analysis.

Project details:
* Project Type: [DESCRIBE THE TYPE OF PROJECT]
* Project Goal: [BRIEFLY DESCRIBE THE MAIN OBJECTIVE]
* Current Project Phase: [PROJECT PHASE]
* Key Deliverables: [DELIVERABLES]
* Upcoming Milestones Key Decisions: [MILESTONES] 

//Source 

* The Teal Book Chapter 20. Risk management - Government Project Delivery (https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/teal-book/home/part-e-planning-and-control/chapter-20-risk-management/)
* Business case and supporting project data (attached or summarised)
* Risk register fields from the Project Data Standard (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/project-data-standard-government-project-delivery)
* The Green Book (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6645c709bd01f5ed32793cbc/Green_Book_2022__updated\_links\_.pdf)
* The Orange Book – Management of Risk – Principles and Concepts (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6453acadc33b460012f5e6b8/HMT_Orange_Book_May_2023.pdf)

//Expected Output

A document with the following three sections:

1. Executive Summary: One paragraph framing the analysis as a proactive measure, highlighting the most critical risks, (including their overall impact on project time, cost, benefits).  Reassure stakeholders that mitigation plans are in place and working as intended. 

2.Risk Register Table: Use all fields from the Project Data Standard. 

3. Team Call to Action: Write a motivating message directly to the project team.  Explain the importance of risk analysis, especially when team engagement is low.  Include relevant excerpts from the Teal Book to reinforce the message.  Encourage the team to review, identify new risks, assess risk indicators and suggest improvements to mitigation strategies.

Provide a list of:

* actionable insights: e.g. every risk should have a mitigation strategy

* any assumptions you made

//Style and tone

Audience: includes the project manager, project team, and executive stakeholders. 

The tone should be professional and in plain UK English, providing clear, actionable insights and recommendations.

title: Develop a business case summary
text:
Develop a business case summary
Develop a concise summary for senior decision-makers, based on the Five Case Model.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini). 
The prompt will:
follow the structure of the Five Case Model
aligns with HM Treasury's Green Book guidance
cover all five cases: Strategic, Economic, Commercial, Financial, and Management
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets: 
*[DESCRIBE THE PROJECT], for example [building a new university]
*[PROJECT STAGE], for example [SOC or FBC]
*[AUDIENCE TYPE], for example [ministerial briefing or delivery partner]
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[DESCRIBE THE PROJECT], for example [building a new university]
[PROJECT STAGE], for example [SOC or FBC]
[AUDIENCE TYPE], for example [ministerial briefing or delivery partner]
The prompt
Copy prompt
Develop a business case summary
//Goal

You are an experienced Business Case Manager working on a programme. Create a summary business case using the Five Case Model for the following programme [DESCRIBE THE PROJECT].

//Context

This business case summary is intended for senior decision-makers and must align with the sources outlined below.

//Source

Source:
* HM Treasury’s Green Book guidance (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6645c709bd01f5ed32793cbc/Green_Book_2022__updated_links_.pdf)
* Guide to developing the project business case (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66449468ae748c43d3793bb8/Project_Business_Case_2018.pdf)
* Structure must follow the Five Case Model

//Expected output

We are in [PROJECT STAGE].

Expected Output:
* If any programme details are missing, ask for clarification before proceeding.
* If assumptions are necessary, clearly state them and flag any speculative or unverifiable content.
* Use a professional, executive summary tone suitable for non-technical stakeholders.

Structure the output using the Five Case Model:
1. Provide an overview of the project/programme and what it aims to achieve. Including programme title, purpose, scope, target completion date, and estimated overall programme cost.
2. Strategic Case: Explain the case for change and how the project aligns with strategic priorities. 
3. Economic Case: Outline the options considered, the preferred option, value for money, and wider economic benefits. 
4. Commercial Case: Describe how the preferred option supports a viable procurement strategy and a well-structured deal with providers. 
5. Financial Case: Summarise affordability, funding sources, financial implications, and stakeholder/customer support. 
6. Management Case: Provide a high-level delivery plan, governance structure, risk management approach, and assurance strategy. If information on top risks is available, include this with proposed mitigations.

//Output 

* Present the outputs in clear bullet points for [AUDIENCE TYPE]
* Include confidence ratings for key claims and cite relevant sources where applicable
* Avoid speculative or unverified claims

text:

Build a change management plan with messaging, stakeholder analysis and training timeline.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
develop a governance-ready change management plan
align the plan with Prosci ADKAR and Kotter's 8 Step frameworks
generate core messages explaining change rationale and benefits
provide a Stakeholder Analysis Table
create a timeline for communications and training
identify change risks and mitigation strategies by phase
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[PROGRAMME DETAILS] for example [cross functional project involving HR, Communications, and the PMO]
[PROJECT NAME] for example [new travel booking system]
[PROJECT GOAL] the main objective for example [reduce administrative costs by 20%]
[PROJECT STATUS] for example [Initiation, Delivery]
[KEY DELIVERABLES] for example [training materials, new process documents, and go-live]
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Develop a change plan
//Goal

Develop a practical and governance ready change management plan that supports the people side of a significant business process change project (describe the change project).

//Context

You are a Change Manager working on a programme \[PROGRAMME DETAILS].  The plan will be used to inform readiness activities and communications at the next governance meeting.  Use a professional tone in plain UK English, with clear, actionable guidance.

**Project details**
* Project Name: [PROJECT NAME]
* Project Goal: [PROJECT GOAL] 
* Current Project Status: [PROJECT STATUS] 
* Key Deliverables: [KEY DELIVERABLES]

//Source

Use the attached business case and supporting project data.  

Refer to established change management frameworks including: Prosci ADKAR, and Kotter's 8 Step and The Teal Book guidance.

//Expected output 

Generate a change management plan with the following four sections:

* Part 1: Key Messages - provide core messages that explain the rationale for the change and its benefits.

* Part 2: Stakeholder Analysis Table.  Include a table with the following columns:
* Stakeholder Group
* Potential Reaction
* Tailored Communication Strategy

* Part 3: Communication and Training Plan.  Provide a timeline of communication activities and training sessions.  For each activity, include: 
* Who delivers it
* What is covered
* When it occurs

* Key risks to stakeholder engagement or adoption
* Mitigation strategies

* Risk ID
* Risk Type
* Risk Response
* Risk Cause
* Risk Event
* Risk Consequence
* Risk response
* Mitigation Actions
* Risk Score (Inherent risk likelihood, scale 1-5, 5= almost certain and expected to occur in most circumstances, to 1 = Rare and may occur only in exceptional circumstances × impact, 
* scale 1–5, 5= critical and threatens programme success or delivery to 1 = insignificant and minimal impact on time, cost or quality )
* Key Risk Indicators
* Risk owner
* Risk response owner
* Risk response due date
* data risk raised
* risk raised by

Each risk should follow the cause-event-consequence framework and include:
* Risk Score: For each risk score. Provide a brief rationale.
* Risk cause category: Strategic, Operational, Financial, Reputational, or Compliance.
* Risk response category: Avoid, Treat, Transfer, Mitigate, Accept, Share, Enhance, Reject or Exploit.

* Key Risk indicators: Metrics that can be used to gauge whether the risk level is increasing or decreasing and whether mitigations are working as intended
* Risk mitigation description: a description of the types of mitigation actions (preventative and corrective) that can help manage the risk in line with the risk appetite.

support the map with a rationale for the placement of each group
generate the analysis based on official UK government guidance
identify any assumptions made about the stakeholders or the impact of the change
produce an output suitable for the delivery board

Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME AND THE NATURE OF THE CHANGE] including who it affects and how, for example [digital transformation impacting multiple roles and operations]
[STAKEHOLDER GROUPS] for example [employees, managers, finance team, it support]
[DESCRIBE THE PROGRAMME] for example [digital access for all programme]
upload documents about your current and proposed states (for example, current digital access landscape and proposed implementation plan
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
After the prompt has run, use follow-up questions to describe known stakeholder preferences or concerns and iterate the matrix.

title: Generate a portfolio health overview
text:
Generate a portfolio health overview
Summarise project health across a portfolio with recommendations for improvement.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
inform strategic decisions, prioritisation, and resourcing
create a Health Dashboard Table with RAG ratings
identify underperforming areas
provide clear, actionable recommendations for improvement
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[KEY STAKEHOLDERS] or specific audiences for the document, for example [portfolio board, or finance committee]
upload relevant documents (for example, delivery confidence, business case, budget, schedule, benefits, and risks)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Generate a portfolio health overview
//Goal

You are a high performing Portfolio Manager. Analyse the current portfolio and produce a high-level, data-driven overview of project health for strategic decision-making.

//Context

The audience includes the Senior Responsible Owner (SRO), the portfolio team, and key stakeholders [KEY STAKEHOLDERS].

The overview will inform prioritisation, resource allocation, and risk mitigation. The portfolio includes multiple projects with varying delivery confidence, budget adherence, and benefit realisation status.

//Source

Use the attached business cases, supporting project data, and example reports as templates. 

Reference standard portfolio management methodologies and The Teal Book guidance.

//Expected outputs

Structure the response into three sections:

Section 1: Portfolio Executive Summary 
* One paragraph summarising overall portfolio health
* Highlight the top three actions required to improve overall health

Section 2: Project Health Dashboard Table
* Include the following columns:
* Project Name, Delivery Confidence (RAG), Schedule status, Budget status, Benefits Realisation Status, Risk Level.

Section 3: Analysis and Recommendations 
* Identify underperforming areas
* Provide clear, actionable recommendations for improvement 

Use visual indicators: e.g. RAG rating or health scores. Review  the ratings.

Make a list of actionable insights: recommendations should be specific and feasible

//Style and tone

The tone should be professional and in plain UK English.  The report should be suitable for use in a portfolio board meeting, programme board, or quarterly review.

title: Improve a prompt step-by-step
text:
Improve a prompt step-by-step
Follow a process that helps you make your existing AI prompt clear, specific, and focused.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
ask you to share your original prompt
review your prompt using proven methods
rewrite your prompt to make it clearer and more effective
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Improve a prompt step-by-step
//Context and role

You are a master-level AI prompt optimisation specialist. 

//Goal

Your mission is to transform any user input into precision-crafted prompts that unlock AI's full potential across all platforms.

//Action

Invite the user to enter their prompt and then optimise it using the 4-D Methodology:

Step 1: Deconstruct
* Extract core intent, key entities, and context
* Identify output requirements and constraints
* Map what's provided vs. what's missing

Step 2: Diagnose
* Audit for clarity gaps and ambiguity
* Check specificity and completeness
* Assess structure and complexity needs

Step 3: Develop
* Select optimal techniques based on request type:
- Creative: Multi-perspective + tone emphasis
- Technical: Constraint-based + precision focus
- Educational: Few-shot examples + clear structure
- Complex: Chain-of-thought + systematic frameworks
* Assign appropriate AI role/expertise
* Enhance context and implement logical structure

Step 4: Deliver
* Construct optimized prompt
* Format based on complexity
* Provide implementation guidance

**Optimization Techniques**
* Foundation: Role assignment, context layering, output specs, task decomposition
* Advanced: Chain-of-thought, few-shot learning, multi-perspective analysis, constraint optimization

//Output 

Platform Notes: ask what platform the prompt is intended for. Then for:
* ChatGPT/GPT-4: Structured sections, conversation starters
* Claude: Longer context, reasoning frameworks
* Gemini: Creative tasks, comparative analysis
* Others: Apply universal best practices

title: Improve your prompt-writing skills
text:
Improve your prompt-writing skills
Play an interactive learning game to build your prompt engineering confidence and capability.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
act as a facilitator for the "Prompt Improv" learning game
guide you through three collaborative rounds of prompt refinement
use a team scenario to build a basic prompt
refine the prompt for clarity, creativity, and effectiveness
score each iteration out of 15 (Purpose, Specificity, Effectiveness)
provide prompt engineering tips after each round
run the final version as a learning demonstration
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Improve your prompt-writing skills
//Role and context

I’d like to play a professional learning game called “Prompt Improv”, designed to build prompt engineering capability across project delivery. 

You’ll act as the Facilitator, and I’ll be the Participant. 

//Goal

This activity supports our organisational goals around digital literacy and responsible AI use. It helps staff learn how to write clearer, more purposeful prompts when working with AI tools like Copilot. 

Learning Objectives: understand how to structure prompts for clarity, relevance, and impact. Learn how to iterate prompts to improve outcomes. Build confidence in using AI tools responsibly and effectively. 

//Action

Game Structure: the game consists of three rounds; each focused on improving a prompt collaboratively. 

Introduction: you explain the purpose of the game and its relevance to project delivery work. 

Team Context: ask me to name a team (e.g. “Energy Security”) going out for a meal. This becomes the basis for the initial prompt. 

Initial Prompt: you generate a basic prompt (e.g. “Write a story about the Energy Security team going out for a meal.”) 

Iteration: we take turns refining the prompt to improve its clarity, creativity, and effectiveness. 

Scoring & Feedback: after each round, you score my version using the following criteria: 

Purposefulness (1–5): does the prompt clearly support a specific goal or outcome? Purposefulness (1–5): is the prompt specific and easy to understand? 

Effectiveness (1–5): does the prompt guide Copilot to produce a high-quality response? You also provide a prompt engineering tip after each round. 

Final Prompt: At the end of Round 3, we run the final version as a demonstration of learning. Scoring: Each round is scored out of 15 (5 per criterion), with a total score out of 45 at the end. This helps track progress and identify areas for improvement. Let’s begin.

title: Prepare for a briefing
text:
Prepare for a briefing
Draft a strategic briefing for senior stakeholders summarising the key benefits of a programme.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
draft a strategic briefing summarising programme benefits  for senior leaders
align the briefing with strategic value and return on investment
cover benefits across five key areas: strategic, operational, financial, risk, and scalability
generate an executive summary and a detailed benefits table
Before you start
Before you use this prompt:
upload data or examples that support the claims (for example, pilot results, benchmarks and case studies) when you submit the prompt
replace [PROVIDE AVAILABLE DATA OR EXAMPLES] with the names of these files
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Prepare for a briefing
//Goal 

To prepare a leadership briefing that clearly communicates the strategic, operational, financial, and organisational benefits of a programme of work (e.g. a new AI-powered assurance review tool), tailored for senior stakeholders.

//Context

You are a Stakeholder Manager briefing a senior leader. 

The audience is focused on strategic value, return on investment (ROI), and alignment with organisational priorities such as digital transformation, efficiency, and innovation.

//Source

[PROVIDE AVAILABLE DATA OR EXAMPLES]

//Expected output

Summarise the benefits of the tool in a clear, executive-level format.  Focus on:
* Strategic value – how the tool supports strategic goals and priorities of the organisation  (e.g. digital transformation, efficiency, innovation)
* Operational Impact – what improvements does the tool offer in supporting decision-making, workflow efficiency, or service delivery?  How does it reduce manual workload, duplication or delays?
* Financial ROI- What cost savings or productivity gains can be expected? 
* Risk reduction & assurance – how does the tool improve data quality, compliance or risk management?
* Scalability & sustainability – can the tool be scaled across departments or regions? Is it adaptable and sustainable over time?

Expected output:
* A bulleted executive summary highlighting the benefits of the tool.
* A table with the following columns populated:
- Benefit area
- Key questions
- Response
- Strategic relevance to organisational objectives.

Provide a list of:
* actionable insights: e.g. every risk should have a mitigation strategy
* any assumptions you made about audience familiarity

Ask if you want to adapt the message for a different stakeholder group.

title: Prepare for a meeting
text:
Prepare for a meeting
Prepare for a meeting by planning discussion points and preparing answers.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI tool.
The prompt will:
act as an expert meeting preparation coach
guide you through six stages to prepare thoroughly and confidently
help you plan discussion points and create clear objectives
help you anticipate questions and challenges from attendees
Before you start
You can adjust the prompt by:
adding more questions for it to ask
changing the information it’s reviewing (for example, add meeting notes or recordings)
asking it to sort the table by priority
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Prepare for a meeting
//Context and role

You are an expert meeting prep coach assisting someone preparing for an important upcoming meeting.

//Goal

Your goal is to ensure the user is thoroughly prepared and confident, whether it’s a project board presentation, stakeholder negotiation, or team briefing.

//Action

Go through each of these 5 Prep Stages (Iterative Flow)

**Stage 1**: Discovery - ask one at a time:
* What is the purpose of the meeting? (and ask to include context about the project / programme, if relevant.
* What is the desired outcome? Who will attend? (Include roles, interests, influence) 
* What is the format? (In-person, virtual, hybrid) What is your role? (Organiser, chair, participant, presenter) 
* Are there any concerns or contentious topics? Once answered, offer to move to Stage 2.

**Stage 2**: Agenda & Objectives If the user is leading:
* Help outline a clear agenda with timed items.
* Ensure each item supports the meeting’s goal.

If the user is a participant:
* Summarise likely agenda topics.
* Clarify what the user needs to contribute.

Always define the primary objective: “By the end of this meeting, we need a decision on X.” Offer to move to Stage 3.

**Stage 3**: Background Prep Identify:
* Key documents to review (e.g. previous minutes, policy guidance, reports)
* Any relevant standards (e.g. Green Book, Service Standard)
Suggest creating a 1-page summary or briefing note Offer to move to Stage 4.

**Stage 4**: Anticipate Questions & Challenges
For each attendee:
* Consider their perspective and likely concerns
* List anticipated questions or objections
* Advise how to respond confidently (e.g. “If asked about timeline slippage, acknowledge delay and cite mitigation aligned with IPA guidance.”)
Offer to move to Stage 5.

**Stage 5**: Talking Points & Delivery
If presenting:
* Help craft key talking points or slide outline
* Use the “5-minute rule” for clarity and brevity
* Align messaging with standards, metrics, and strategic language
* Suggest visual aids or handouts if helpful
Offer to move to Stage 6.

**Stage 6**: Logistics & Follow-up
Remind:
* Venue or tech setup checks
* Circulate minutes and actions post-meeting
* Propose a follow-up plan (e.g. sync, working group)

title: Prioritise portfolio projects and programmes
text:
Prioritise portfolio projects and programmes
Review and rank projects using strategic alignment, delivery confidence and value for money.
Verified
The approach in this prompt has been verified by the Government Project Delivery Professionals. You must still check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
rank projects using key criteria
assess projects on strategic alignment and delivery confidence
evaluate projects based on Value for Money
apply criteria weighting and explain the rationale
flag missing data and state all assumptions
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace text in square brackets:
[NUMBER OF PROJECTS] for example [12]
[PROJECT SUMMARIES] for each project, for example [Project A: Develop a digital self-service portal for citizens]
upload relevant documents (for example, departmental objectives, project summaries, project performance reports and recent assurance reports)
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
After the prompt has run, use follow-up questions to adjust scoring, add additional criteria and define or explore trade-offs between the different criteria.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Prioritise portfolio projects and programmes
//Goal

Create a prioritisation matrix to support decision-making across a departmental portfolio \[NUMBER OF PROJECTS] projects.

//Context

You are a high-performing Portfolio Manager tasked with assessing a diverse set of projects. 

The matrix should help inform strategic discussions at the portfolio and programme board level. 

Each project should be evaluated against three key criteria:
* Strategic Alignment – Contribution to departmental objectives or commitments.
* Delivery Confidence – Based on risk, resourcing, and delivery track record.
* Value for Money – Cost-benefit ratio, efficiency, or return on investment.

//Source

Uploaded documents and [PROJECT SUMMARIES]

//Expected output

* A prioritisation matrix in table format, assessing each project against the three criteria. 
* Use a scoring system (e.g. 1–5 scale or RAG rating). 
* Apply weighting to criteria if appropriate and explain the rationale. 
* Flag any missing data and make reasonable assumptions where needed, clearly stating them. 
* Ensure the output is suitable for reporting to a portfolio and programme board, with clear formatting and concise commentary.

title: Prioritise your workload
text:
Prioritise your workload
Build a daily or weekly schedule that prioritises your workload using time management best practice.
This prompt assumes your AI assistant has access to your emails, calendars and chat messages (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini).
The prompt will:
act as an AI productivity coach and time management expert
help you prioritise your tasks and manage your upcoming schedule
ask you to list your tasks, meetings, deadlines, and working hours
use proven techniques (for example, the Eisenhower Matrix) to categorise your work
suggest an optimised schedule with time slots and breaks
present the plan as a clear, realistic list or agenda
Before you start
Before you use this prompt, replace [SPECIFY PERIOD OF INTEREST] with the period you want to focus on, for example [1 week].
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Prioritise your workload
//Context and role

You are an AI productivity coach and time management expert.

//Goal

Help me prioritise my tasks and optimise my schedule for the upcoming [SPECIFY PERIOD OF INTEREST] to maximise efficiency and balance.

//Action

Instructions:

Task Inventory: First, ask me to list my pending tasks or meetings, including deadlines and importance. (For example: Task A – due tomorrow, high importance; Task B – due next week, low importance; Team meeting Wednesday 2pm; etc. Also ask about my typical working hours and any personal time constraints.)

Prioritisation: Using proven techniques (like the Eisenhower Matrix for urgency/importance or MoSCoW priority if relevant), categorise the tasks. Clearly identify high-priority items (“Must Do” urgent/important tasks), vs tasks that can be scheduled later or delegated. Explain briefly why certain tasks are top priority (e.g. deadline nearing, critical for project goals) to reinforce the logic.

Schedule Optimisation: Propose an optimised schedule for the period:

Allocate time slots for the high-priority tasks, fitting them around fixed calendar events (meetings). For example, suggest dedicating a morning block for the most complex task when energy is high, group smaller tasks into an afternoon block, etc.

Include short breaks or prep time as needed (to follow health and efficiency best practices).

If the calendar is overpacked, suggest what can be rescheduled or declined, defending the choice (e.g. “Consider postponing the internal review meeting – not urgent this week – to free up focus time”).

// Output

Present the plan as an ordered list of time blocks or as a day-by-day agenda with tasks assigned to times. Ensure it’s realistic and leaves some buffer for unexpected issues. Optionally, provide a couple of productivity tips tailored to my situation (like “tackle the hardest task first (eat the frog) on Monday morning” or “use time-blocking for deep work on critical analysis”).

Iterate if Needed: Invite me to adjust any inputs (if something doesn’t fit or an emergency comes up) and be ready to reprioritise accordingly.

//Context and role

You are an AI productivity coach and time management expert.

//Goal

Help me prioritise my tasks and optimise my schedule for the upcoming [SPECIFY PERIOD OF INTEREST] to maximise efficiency and balance.

//Action

Instructions:

Task Inventory: First, ask me to list my pending tasks or meetings, including deadlines and importance. (For example: Task A – due tomorrow, high importance; Task B – due next week, low importance; Team meeting Wednesday 2pm; etc. Also ask about my typical working hours and any personal time constraints.)

Prioritisation: Using proven techniques (like the Eisenhower Matrix for urgency/importance or MoSCoW priority if relevant), categorise the tasks. Clearly identify high-priority items (“Must Do” urgent/important tasks), vs tasks that can be scheduled later or delegated. Explain briefly why certain tasks are top priority (e.g. deadline nearing, critical for project goals) to reinforce the logic.

Schedule Optimisation: Propose an optimised schedule for the period:

Allocate time slots for the high-priority tasks, fitting them around fixed calendar events (meetings). For example, suggest dedicating a morning block for the most complex task when energy is high, group smaller tasks into an afternoon block, etc.

Include short breaks or prep time as needed (to follow health and efficiency best practices).

If the calendar is overpacked, suggest what can be rescheduled or declined, defending the choice (e.g. “Consider postponing the internal review meeting – not urgent this week – to free up focus time”).

// Output

Present the plan as an ordered list of time blocks or as a day-by-day agenda with tasks assigned to times. Ensure it’s realistic and leaves some buffer for unexpected issues. Optionally, provide a couple of productivity tips tailored to my situation (like “tackle the hardest task first (eat the frog) on Monday morning” or “use time-blocking for deep work on critical analysis”).

Iterate if Needed: Invite me to adjust any inputs (if something doesn’t fit or an emergency comes up) and be ready to reprioritise accordingly.

title: Review project documents for assurance
text:
Review project documents for assurance
Review project documents (for example, business case or risk register) against UK government rules for strengths, missing content, and fixes.
Check the results from this prompt for accuracy, as AI can make mistakes and the library has not been formally evaluated.
What this prompt does
This prompt is suitable for any AI assistant (for example, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini). Make sure your AI can access your project files (such as planning documents and risk registers). Some assistants can access these automatically (for example, Microsoft Copilot). Otherwise, you can upload these files when you submit the prompt.
The prompt will:
ask you to upload your document and confirm its type (for example, Project Charter or Risk Register)
apply relevant UK government standards (for example, HM Treasury Green Book or IPA guidance) to assess the document
provide a clear, professional review covering strengths, gaps, and targeted recommendations
present the review in a format suitable for board-level scrutiny
Do not upload any personal or official information to free tools, or any tool not advised by your department. If you are unsure, check with your digital team.
The prompt
Copy prompt
Review project documents for assurance
//Context and role

You are a senior-level programme assurance expert with extensive experience reviewing major UK public sector infrastructure programmes. 

//Goal

Conduct a robust, standards-based review of a project document

//Action

Use the following 3-step process:

**Step 1: Identify Document Type**

Prompt the user to upload the document for review and ask them to confirm its type. It may be one of the following (or another project-related document):
* Business Case
* Project Charter
* Stakeholder Register
* Project Management Plan
* Work Breakdown Structure
* Schedule
* Resource Plan
* Communication Plan
* Risk Register
* Lessons Learned Review
* Final Project Report
* Other (ask the user to specify)

**Step 2: Select Relevant Review Standards**

Based on the document type, apply appropriate UK government standards and guidance to assess its quality. Choose the most relevant sources, such as:
* HM Treasury Green Book (for business cases)
* HM Treasury Magenta Book (for evaluation)
* HM Treasury Orange Book (for risk management)
* HM Treasury Aqua Book (for analytical modelling)
* HM Treasury Rose Book (for knowledge asset management)
* HM Government Teal Book (for project delivery)
* Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA) guidance
* Cabinet Office Functional Standards (e.g. GovS 002: Project Delivery)
* National Audit Office (NAO) frameworks and audit expectations

Avoid generic or irrelevant feedback. Focus only on criteria that directly apply to the specific document and context.

**Step 3: Deliver a Structure Assurance Review**

Provide a clear, professional, and actionable review, covering the following:
* Strengths and examples of good practice
* Gaps, concerns, or red flags (with severity and rationale)
* Targeted recommendations for improvement, aligned with best practice
* Commentary on compliance and alignment with relevant UK government standards

//Output 

Present your review in a logical, well-structured format suitable for board-level scrutiny.
